caption: Clients — Client 360
vo: Every Genesis entity serving the same client, but from one record. That's Client 360. One golden record per client, and everything Genesis does with them, in one place.

caption: Priya, a relationship manager, meets a new client at the branch
vo: Here's our story. Priya, a relationship manager, meets a new client at the branch. Kavya Beeharry, the wife of an existing client, wants to invest with Genesis Wealth.

caption: Sign in as Priya Ramdin — Relationship Manager
vo: So Priya signs in. She'll own this client, and the relationship.

caption: First, a household for the family
vo: Before Kavya herself, Priya sets up a household for the family. That's where the family's value adds up.

caption: A household or corporate group adds up its members’ relationship value
vo: A household or corporate group adds up its members' relationship value. Members join from their own client record, and a corporate group also has a lending limit.

caption: Now the client herself: Clients ▸ Parties ▸ New
vo: Now the client herself. Open Clients, then Parties, and click New. One party per person or company, shared group-wide.

caption: Identity: the form shows the individual fields for a person
vo: For a person, the form shows the individual fields. Choose Organisation instead, and it asks for the legal name, BRN and sector.

caption: The ID number is personal data: it is stored encrypted and shown masked
vo: The ID number is personal data, so it's stored encrypted and shown masked. And clients must be eighteen or over, checked on save.

caption: Contact details, preferred language and channel
vo: Then her contact details, preferred language and channel. And Priya puts her straight into the household she just created, so the family's value adds up from day one.

caption: A client can have several addresses and phones
vo: Clients often have more than one address or phone. Here Priya adds a correspondence address, a PO box in Quatre Bornes, and marks it as verified and preferred.

caption: Record her marketing consent: one record per purpose and channel
vo: Next, her marketing consent. It's one record per purpose and channel, in line with the Data Protection Act two thousand seventeen.

caption: Marketing campaigns only reach clients with a granted consent
vo: Why bother? Because campaigns only reach clients with a granted consent. No consent, a withdrawal, do not contact, or an open complaint, and she's suppressed.

caption: Link related people: spouse, director, shareholder, beneficial owner, guarantor…
vo: Now the people around her. Spouse, director, shareholder, beneficial owner, guarantor. Here, Priya links Kavya to her husband, Rohan Beeharry, an existing client.

caption: Open her relationship with the entity she will deal with
vo: Then Priya opens Kavya's relationship with the entity she'll actually deal with, Genesis Wealth. There's one relationship per Genesis entity, so each part of the group tracks its own.

caption: The relationship lifecycle: Prospect ▸ Onboarding ▸ Active ▸ Dormant ▸ Closed ▸ Exited
vo: Every relationship moves through a lifecycle, from Prospect through Onboarding, Active, Dormant and Closed, to Exited.

caption: She has agreed to go ahead: move her to Onboarding
vo: Kavya's agreed to go ahead, so Priya drags her to Onboarding.

caption: Can she become Active straight away?
vo: But can she go Active straight away?

caption: No — the move is refused: her KYC is not approved yet
vo: No. The move is refused, because her KYC isn't approved yet. Once the KYC and Compliance team approves her case, it goes through.

caption: Closing a relationship asks for the closing date; Exited also asks for a note
vo: Closing a relationship asks for the closing date, and Exited also wants a note. All set up in the Builder, no code.

caption: Back on her client record: everything is linked
vo: Back on Kavya's client record, everything is linked. Her email, phone and address are right there in the header.

caption: Related: her relationship, household, address, consent and spouse
vo: The Related tab shows her relationship, household, address, consent and spouse. Click any row to open it.

caption: The calculated Client 360 figures fill themselves in
vo: And the Client 360 figures fill themselves in. KYC, not started yet. Marketing consent, yes.

caption: A week later she calls: no more marketing emails
vo: A week later, Kavya calls. No more marketing emails, please. So Priya opens the consent, clicks Edit, sets the status to Withdrawn, and adds the date.

caption: Marketing consent is now No and she is suppressed from marketing
vo: Now marketing consent shows No, and she's suppressed. The latest decision per purpose wins, so campaigns skip her automatically.

caption: Now an established client: Christelle Leclézio
vo: Now let's look at an established client, Christelle Leclézio. Any client conversation starts right here.

caption: ID number and income band are masked for a relationship manager
vo: Her ID number and income band are masked. There's no Reveal link, because a relationship manager can't view personal data.

caption: Client 360 figures: wealth AUM, fund holdings, total relationship value in MUR and USD
vo: And here's the full picture. Wealth AUM, fund holdings, total relationship value in Mauritian rupees and US dollars, products held, open applications and complaints, KYC status and AML risk.

caption: Next-best actions open, and the suitable product risk ceiling from her risk profile
vo: Open next-best actions, and the product risk ceiling from her risk profile. Every figure recalculates when a linked record changes.

caption: Related: everything Genesis does with her, across every entity
vo: Related shows everything Genesis does with her, across every entity. KYC case, risk profile, fund holdings, next-best actions, consents, meetings and events.

caption: Rows owned by another desk that you may not open show as “restricted”
vo: Some rows belong to another desk and show as restricted. Ask Compliance if you need them. Nothing is hidden silently.

caption: Activity: log the call you just had with her
vo: Priya's just had a call with Christelle about her maturing bond, so she logs it on the Activity tab. Calls, meetings, emails and notes all stay on the client record.

caption: The call is on her timeline, with who logged it and when
vo: There it is on her timeline, who logged it, and when.

caption: Compliance may view personal data — on demand, and audited
vo: So who can see personal data? Compliance can, on demand, and audited.

caption: Sign in as Fatima Hossenbux — Compliance Officer
vo: Fatima Hossenbux signs in, a Compliance Officer. Her role holds the view personal data permission.

caption: She also sees the ID number masked — with a Reveal link
vo: Even Fatima sees Kavya's ID number masked at first, but with a Reveal link. Personal data only shows when someone deliberately asks.

caption: Revealed — and recorded in the tamper-evident audit trail
vo: Revealed. And recorded in the tamper-evident audit trail.

caption: The Audit tab shows who revealed which field, and when
vo: The Audit tab shows who revealed which field, and when, right alongside every change, stage move and approval.

caption: What you learned
vo: So, the party is the golden record, and everything else links to it. Next up, KYC and Compliance, approving the case that unlocks Kavya's relationship.
